questions.prompt: Do you carry paper and pens with you when you go out?

answers.basic: Usually I just take my phone. I sometimes bring a small notebook to a badminton session if I want to write down a few things to cover. It's handy on court because I can glance at a short list between drills without getting distracted by a notification.

questions.prompt: Do people still keep handwritten letters today?

answers.basic: Yes, especially letters from relatives or people they don't see often. A handwritten note feels personal, so I can see why someone would keep it for years. A friend might keep a letter from home because even the handwriting can remind them of the person who sent it.

questions.prompt: Do you still write physical letters?

answers.basic: Hardly ever. I send messages for most things, but I'd still write a few lines by hand in a birthday card. A card gives me a good reason to slow down and write something specific about the person I'm giving it to.

questions.prompt: What did you like to do with paper as a child?

answers.basic: I used to fold paper planes and change the wings to see how far they'd go. Half the fun was seeing whose plane would land first. I liked that a small fold could make one plane turn sharply while another one flew almost straight across the room.

questions.prompt: Have you made any crafts with paper?

answers.basic: Yes, I made simple paper boats and planes as a child. I remember trying to make a boat strong enough to float in a bowl of water. I enjoyed seeing whether a different fold made it float longer, even when it sank almost as soon as I let go.
